conclusion: The 1934 Erdos-Turan bound g(k) <= 3*2^(k-1)-1 is still the record and the S-unit literature (Gyory-Stewart-Tijdeman 1986 via Evertse) is quantitatively worse at 49^k, but it isolates the single lever: g(k) <= 2 + N(k), where N(k) counts coprime S-unit solutions of lambda x + mu y = nu z, so a uniform exp(o(k)) bound on N(k) implies Erdos #126. That route is not blocked -- Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman 1988 only forbids polynomial bounds, leaving the whole window exp(sqrt(k/log k)) .. exp(o(k)) open, every point of which settles the problem.
confidence: Lean hard on the reduction and on the incumbent bound: I read Erdos-Turan 1934 and Gyory-Stewart-Tijdeman I in full, and the reduction is their section 3 plus one elementary step I proved. Lean less on two numbers -- the Erdos-Suranyi 2^k+1 and the Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman constant 1/8 -- which are secondary citations via Furedi-Gyarmati (arXiv:2602.07545, Feb 2026) and were not checked against the originals. The claim that nothing improves f(n) >> log n is a targeted-search negative, corroborated by two independent recent surveys (the erdosproblems.com/126 page and that Feb 2026 paper), not an exhaustive one.
